# Usage {#sec-en-usage}

[🇩🇪 Auf Deutsch lesen](../de/usage.html){.btn .btn-sm .btn-outline-secondary style="float:right"}

This chapter covers installation, configuration, and daily operation of gdrive-fuse.

## Installation & Build {#sec-en-usage-install}

### System Requirements

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Ubuntu / Debian

```bash
sudo apt-get install \
  build-essential cmake pkg-config \
  libfuse3-dev libssl-dev \
  rustup
```

#### Fedora / RHEL

```bash
sudo dnf install \
  gcc-c++ cmake pkgconfig \
  fuse3-devel openssl-devel \
  rust cargo
```

#### Arch Linux

```bash
sudo pacman -S base-devel cmake fuse3 openssl rust
```

:::

Minimum versions:

| Component | Minimum |
|---|---|
| CMake | ≥ 3.20 |
| GCC / Clang | ≥ 12 / ≥ 15 (C++20) |
| Rust | ≥ 1.75 (Edition 2021) |
| libfuse3 | ≥ 3.10 |
| OpenSSL | ≥ 1.1 |

### Get the Source

```bash
git clone https://github.com/the78mole/gdrive-fuse.git
cd gdrive-fuse
```

### Build

The top-level `Makefile` delegates to the respective build systems:

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `make build` | Debug build for all clients |
| `make build-cpp` | C++ only (CMake debug) |
| `make build-rust` | Rust only (`cargo build`) |
| `make build-release` | Release build for all clients |
| `make format` | `clang-format` + `cargo fmt` |
| `make lint` | `clang-tidy` + `cargo clippy` |

```bash
# Recommended first build:
make build
```

On the first run, CMake automatically downloads all C++ dependencies
(`nlohmann/json`, `spdlog`, `cpr`) via `FetchContent`.

## Google Cloud Credentials

### Create a Project

1. Open the [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com/).
2. Create a new project or select an existing one.
3. **APIs & Services → Library** → enable the *Google Drive API*.
4. **APIs & Services → Credentials** → *Create Credentials* →
   *OAuth client ID*.
5. Application type: **Desktop app**.
6. Download the JSON file and save it as `credentials.json` in the project
   directory.

::: {.callout-warning}
`credentials.json` and `.gdrive_tokens.json` are listed in `.gitignore` and
must **never** be committed to the repository.
:::

### Extract Values

```bash
# Read client ID and secret from credentials.json:
CLIENT_ID=$(jq -r '.installed.client_id' credentials.json)
CLIENT_SECRET=$(jq -r '.installed.client_secret' credentials.json)
```

Alternatively, set them as environment variables (Rust client):

```bash
export CLIENT_ID=<your-client-id>
export CLIENT_SECRET=<your-client-secret>
```

## FUSE Group Setup

To allow a regular user to mount FUSE filesystems:

```bash
# Add user to fuse group (one-time):
sudo usermod -aG fuse $USER
# Start a new session or:
newgrp fuse
```

For `allow_other` support (other users can see the filesystem):

```bash
# Edit /etc/fuse.conf:
echo "user_allow_other" | sudo tee -a /etc/fuse.conf
```

## Mounting

### C++ Client

```bash
# Create mount point:
mkdir -p ~/mnt/gdrive-fuse

# Run manually:
./clients/cpp/build/gdrive-fuse \
  --client-id "$CLIENT_ID" \
  --client-secret "$CLIENT_SECRET" \
  ~/mnt/gdrive-fuse

# Via Make:
make run-cpp
```

On first start, a browser window opens for OAuth2 authorization.
The token is saved to `~/.gdrive_tokens.json` and reused automatically on
subsequent starts.

### Rust Client

```bash
./clients/rust/target/debug/gdrive-fuse-rs \
  --client-id "$CLIENT_ID" \
  --client-secret "$CLIENT_SECRET" \
  ~/mnt/gdrive-fuse

# Or using environment variables:
make run-rust
```

### Command-Line Options

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### C++ Client

```
Usage: gdrive-fuse [options] <mountpoint>

Options:
  --client-id <id>         OAuth2 client ID (required)
  --client-secret <secret> OAuth2 client secret (required)
  --debug                  Enable debug logging
  --help                   Show help message

FUSE options may be passed after the mountpoint.
```

#### Rust Client

```
Usage: gdrive-fuse-rs [OPTIONS] <MOUNTPOINT>

Arguments:
  <MOUNTPOINT>  Mount point directory

Options:
      --client-id <CLIENT_ID>         OAuth2 client ID [env: CLIENT_ID]
      --client-secret <CLIENT_SECRET> OAuth2 client secret [env: CLIENT_SECRET]
  -d, --debug                         Enable debug logging
  -h, --help                          Print help
  -V, --version                       Print version
```

:::

## Normal Operation

After a successful mount, Google Drive is accessible as an ordinary directory:

```bash
# List contents:
ls ~/mnt/gdrive-fuse

# Read a file:
cat ~/mnt/gdrive-fuse/document.txt

# Copy from Drive to local disk:
cp ~/mnt/gdrive-fuse/report.pdf ~/Downloads/

# Upload a file:
cp ~/Downloads/new-file.xlsx ~/mnt/gdrive-fuse/

# Delete a file:
rm ~/mnt/gdrive-fuse/old-file.txt
```

::: {.callout-note}
Google Docs files (`.gdoc`, `.gsheet`, …) appear as shortcut files containing
a link to the web interface. They cannot be edited directly.
:::

## Unmounting

```bash
# Via Make:
make stop

# Manually:
fusermount3 -u ~/mnt/gdrive-fuse
```

## Performance Benchmarks

The repository includes a benchmark script that compares the C++ and Rust
clients (requires [hyperfine](https://github.com/sharkdp/hyperfine)):

```bash
make bench
# or directly:
bash benchmarks/run.sh
```

## Troubleshooting

### "Transport endpoint is not connected"

The filesystem was not cleanly unmounted. Force unmount:

```bash
fusermount3 -uz ~/mnt/gdrive-fuse
```

### "fuse: device not found" / Permission denied

The `fuse` group is missing or `fuse.ko` is not loaded:

```bash
# Load the module:
sudo modprobe fuse

# Check group membership:
groups $USER | grep fuse
```

### Token expired / "invalid_grant"

Delete the stored tokens and re-authenticate:

```bash
rm ~/.gdrive_tokens.json
# Restart the client
```

### Enable Debug Logging

```bash
# C++:
./gdrive-fuse --debug --client-id ... --client-secret ... ~/mnt/gdrive-fuse

# Rust:
RUST_LOG=debug ./gdrive-fuse-rs ...
```
